true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

The legacy flexbox properties -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group use a 1-based initial value, while the standard order property uses 0. Emitting the same $val for both means the mixin does not provide equivalent behavior: for example @include order(1) has no effect in browsers using the legacy box syntax, and other values are shifted by one relative to modern flexbox. Since this mixin is intended to abstract ordering for the header layout, emit $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same problem. The legacy box-ordinal-group properties are 1-based, while the mixin passes the 0-based order value through unchanged, which causes incorrect ordering in older browsers.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it never runs

ActiveModel::Serializer decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`. This guard is named `include_website_name` (no trailing `?`), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is emitted for every serialized user, including users with no website (as `null`). The intended `website.present?` condition has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, or (better, see the trust-level finding) move `website_name` into `untrusted_attributes`.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name leaks a website that untrusted_attributes deliberately hides

`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that a TL0 user's profile fields are not exposed to anonymous visitors (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list and has no such guard: its `include_website_name` method only checks `website.present?` and, being misnamed, is not called anyway. As a result anonymous visitors now receive `website_name` containing the hidden TL0 user's website host and path, defeating the anti-spam restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and make the include check honour `restrict_user_fields?`).

Gating the website block on model.website_name hides websites the serializer cannot parse

The block that renders the globe icon and the website link is now guarded by `{{#if model.website_name}}`. The serializer returns `nil` whenever `URI(website.to_s)` raises (e.g. a URL containing a space such as `http://example.com/my page`), and it is also absent if an endpoint does not include the new attribute. Previously the display name was derived in JS from `model.website` (`website.split('/')[2]`), so such a user still saw the globe and a link. Now the website silently disappears from the profile even though `model.website` is present. Gate on `model.website` and fall back to a derived name, or make the serializer always return a non-nil name when the website is present.

untested: website_name is not added to the untrusted attributes spec

The `untrusted_attributes` list still contains only the original attributes. Because `website_name` is not added, there is no test asserting that the new field is omitted for a TL0 user seen as anonymous, so the leak of a hidden website described elsewhere in this review passes the suite. Add `website_name` here; the test should fail until the serializer guards that attribute.

The equal-length subdomain branch of website_name is never exercised

The three new examples cover `website_host == discourse_host`, the `else` branch, and the parent-domain case. None exercises the `elsif` branch (`website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && ... > 2`), i.e. the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` case named in the code comment, which is the most complex branch. The nil/invalid-website case (host cannot be parsed) is also untested.

The equivalence check removes only the first label of each host and compares the rest. For hosts whose public suffix has more than one label this is wrong: with website `http://foo.co.uk/post` and instance `bar.co.uk`, comparing `['foo','co','uk'][1..-1].join` with `['bar','co','uk'][1..-1].join` yields `co.uk` for both, so it reports the domains as the same and shows the full path `foo.co.uk/post`, even though `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` are unrelated registrable domains. Use a real registrable-domain/public-suffix comparison, or only treat the website as a subdomain of the instance when it actually ends with `.` + instance host (and vice versa).

true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same bug: `i.content` can be nil in RSS items, so calling `.scrub` on it raises an error. Both also propose falling back to `description`.

postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

Animated GIF downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle

This call passes dimensions `"80%"` together with `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When `optimize` selects the animated path (for a `from` path ending in `.GIF`), `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects a `WxH` value, not a percentage, so the command fails, the loop burns all five attempts, and the oversized GIF is uploaded unchanged. After five failures it exits and `Upload.create_for` is called with the original tempfile, so an image still larger than `max_image_size_kb` (or a partially written file) can be persisted as an upload, with no error returned to the user. There is also no final size check after the loop. Check the downsize result/final size and reject with a clear error instead of silently storing the oversized file.

The PR adds non-trivial branching (image vs non-image, successful downsize, downsize failure, animated GIFs, oversized files, API url uploads) without any specs. Tests exercising these paths would have caught the overridden `downsize` signature and the invalid `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` command. Add coverage for `create_upload` downsize behavior and the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` overload.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET with no signed token

The new route is a plain GET that calls `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which changes the logged-in user's `topic_users.notification_level`. Because the URL has no signed per-recipient token and GET requests are not CSRF-protected, any third-party page can embed/fetch this URL for a logged-in user and silently mute or downgrade notifications for a topic; mail scanners/link prefetchers can trigger the same effect. Use a signed token and/or a POST/confirmation flow for the mutation.

Repeated unsubscribe requests progressively downgrade the topic

The new level depends on the current level: watching/tracking becomes regular, while regular/muted becomes muted. A page refresh, double-click, or a fetched-link retry therefore runs the mutation again and can take a user from watching to regular and then to muted. The unsubscribe target should be deterministic/idempotent (or encoded in a signed link), otherwise retries silently over-mute the topic.

unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link email

The shared server locale string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder` still treats `unsubscribe_url` as optional and only checks `add_unsubscribe_link` when rendering `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. Any caller using `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without the new option, or a non-topic/digest mailer that only supplies `user_preferences_url`, will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and fail to build the email. Default `unsubscribe_url` to the preferences URL, guard the interpolation, or keep the per-topic sentence in a separate conditional string.

No coverage for the new unsubscribe endpoint or per-topic link

The PR adds a destructive controller action and URL but the only spec change adds an unused `unsubscribe_url` to an existing email-builder test. There are no tests that the per-topic URL appears in the email body, that `TopicsController#unsubscribe` updates `notification_level` correctly (including when no TopicUser exists), or that repeated requests do not further downgrade the setting. Add request/controller specs so these behaviors are protected.

Separately, `ENV_FILE` on line 5 is relative to the caller’s current working directory, so running it from the repo root writes to the parent directory’s `.env` rather than the repo `.env`. true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US

The component formats `cacheUpdatedAt` with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the active locale from `useLocale`. Users in other locales get U.S.-formatted dates in an otherwise localized UI. Use the current locale or a shared date formatting helper instead of the literal `"en-US"`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same problem: the date is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' locale rather than the user's locale from useLocale.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache status includes expired cache rows

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates every `CalendarCache` row for the credential without filtering on `expiresAt`, while `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`. Expired rows are not deleted elsewhere, so `cacheUpdatedAt` stays non-null after the cache expires. The UI then shows “Cache Status / Last updated” and “Delete cached data” for a cache that is not actually being served, giving users a misleading view of cache state. Add an `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` predicate or return expiry state explicitly.

Migration backfills every cache row with the deployment time

Adding `updatedAt ... DEFAULT NOW()` sets all pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows to the time the migration runs. Since the new UI displays `_max(updatedAt)` as “Last updated”, every existing cached credential will appear to have been refreshed at deploy time even though the old rows have no real update timestamp. Existing caches will report a false freshness date until each row is rewritten. Consider making the column nullable for legacy rows, backfilling from a meaningful source, or suppressing the status for backfilled rows.

Cache deletion does not invalidate connected calendars query

`deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` callback. Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, and `onSuccess` is optional at this component’s API. In a caller that does not pass an invalidating `onSuccess`, the dropdown continues to render the old `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamp and a delete action for data that no longer exists until the user manually refreshes. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` after successful deletion.

No tests for destructive cache deletion authorization

This PR adds a destructive `deleteCache` mutation and an ownership check, but no tests cover the new handler, the unauthorized path (credential id belonging to another user), or the repository’s `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` behavior (empty ids, multiple cache rows, expired rows). A regression in the ownership check would let a user delete another user’s cache. Add unit/integration tests for authorized and unauthorized deletion and the cache-status query.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Slot end is never checked against working-hour end

`end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour()` and `slotStartTime.minute()` instead of `slotEndTime`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot extending past the working hours when the start is inside the range. In a round-robin event with a fixed host whose availability ends before the event slot's end, a 60-minute slot starting at 10:30 passes a working-hour range ending at 11:00. This should use the slot end time for the upper-bound check.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the end time is computed from slotStartTime when it should come from slotEndTime. The candidate also explains the consequence, that the upper-bound check against working-hour end never catches slots that run past it.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zero-length date override check compares Dayjs objects by identity

The condition `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate Dayjs object instances and is always false. A date override with identical start and end, which is the representation this code is trying to treat as a fully unavailable day, is not handled; for a slot starting exactly at the override start, the other boundary checks also fail to reject it, so a slot can leak through. Use `.isSame()` or compare timestamps.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: dayjs objects are compared with ===, which checks reference identity, so the result is always false. Both recommend using .isSame() instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override path skips busy-time checks

`checkIfIsAvailable` now returns `true` as soon as a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not completely outside it, before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check. Existing bookings or calendar busy times that fall inside a date override are therefore ignored when filtering fixed/loose hosts. A host with an override 10:00-11:00 and a booking 10:00-10:30 will still be offered at 10:00, allowing a double booking. The override check should only decide whether the slot is within the override; busy-time filtering must still run afterward.

Partially overlapping slots are accepted for date overrides

The override containment logic only rejects a slot when it ends at/before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is treated as available, and a slot starting exactly at the override end is also accepted because the final condition uses `isAfter(end)` instead of also rejecting `isSame(end)`. For example, with a fixed host override 10:00-11:00 and an event slot 09:30-10:30 generated from another host, the fixed host check passes even though the fixed host is only available 10:00-11:00. The slot should be available only when `slotStartTime >= overrideStart` and `slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

Working-hours check rejects valid split availability

The working-hours validation uses `find` with a callback that returns true when the slot is outside that particular working-hour range. If a host has two same-day ranges, e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because the second range returns true when `start < workingHour.startTime`. Since this check runs for fixed hosts and personal-event users, split availability becomes largely unavailable. The code should use `some`/`every` to reject only when no same-day range contains the slot.

Date override day filter ignores converted invitee date

`activeOverrides` still filters by comparing the organizer's original `override.start` against `startOfInviteeDay`, without applying the timezone offset computed below. This breaks date overrides when the converted time falls on a different invitee day. Example: 09:30-18:00 Asia/Kolkata on Aug 15 is 21:00 Aug 14-04:30 Aug 15 in America/Los_Angeles, but the override is not active for the invitee Aug 14 day; it is instead applied one day later on Aug 15. The filter needs to use the same converted instant as the minute calculation.

No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides

The only added test checks a personal event with a +30 minute timezone difference, where the override stays on the same invitee day. It does not cover the PR's main behavior: a round-robin event with a fixed host date override, a negative timezone offset/day rollover, or a date override combined with an existing busy booking. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` override/working-hours logic is therefore untested for the cases most likely to regress, including skipping busy times or accepting partially overlapping slots.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry count increment is a lost-update race

Both new increments use reminder.retryCount + 1 with the value read before the Twilio call. If two cron executions (or a retried request) process the same reminder concurrently, both can read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, so a failure is lost. The reminder can then keep retrying past the intended two-failure limit and never be deleted. Use an atomic Prisma increment such as { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } or an equivalent SQL update.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: the retryCount + 1 update reads a stale value, so concurrent runs can lose increments. Both also recommend an atomic Prisma increment, and the candidate notes it applies to both updates, as the golden comment does.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry cleanup deletes non-SMS workflow reminders

The new OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders. WorkflowReminder is shared by email, SMS, and WhatsApp, so any non-SMS row that ever reaches retryCount > 1 (including future code paths that use this shared column) will be deleted by this cron. The branch also ignores the scheduled state, so a scheduled row with retryCount > 1 would be deleted while its external scheduled job still exists. Scope the condition to the intended SMS/failed reminders, for example by including method: WorkflowMethods.SMS and the intended scheduled state.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug as the golden comment. The retryCount > 1 OR branch is missing a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so it deletes non-SMS reminders. The candidate also suggests the same fix.

false_positives.candidate:
Catch increments retries even when the SMS was already scheduled

The try block includes the prisma.workflowReminder.update at lines 169-177 that records a successful Twilio send. If twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but that database update throws, the catch block increments retryCount and leaves scheduled false. The next cron run sends the same SMS again, and the new delete logic can eventually remove the row, losing the referenceId of the already-scheduled Twilio message so it cannot be cancelled. Retry increments should only happen for actual twilio.scheduleSMS failures; persistence errors after a successful send need separate handling.

Missing sendTo or empty message never increments retryCount

If sendTo is missing or message is empty, this condition is false and the loop continues without calling Twilio and without throwing. No retryCount increment occurs, so the reminder remains unscheduled and is picked up again on every cron run forever, which is exactly the infinite-retry behavior this PR is trying to stop. Handle this skip case by incrementing the retry counter, deleting the invalid reminder, or otherwise recording the failure.

No index for the retryCount cleanup query

The cron now runs deleteMany with a predicate on retryCount > 1, but the migration adds no index for retryCount. On a large WorkflowReminder table this OR predicate can force a full scan on every cron invocation, even though almost all rows have retryCount 0. Add an appropriate index (for example a partial index on retryCount > 0, or a composite index with method) to keep the cleanup query efficient.

No tests for the destructive retry cleanup path

The PR adds retry accounting and a deleteMany that permanently removes workflow reminder rows, but no test covers the new behavior. Add tests for: SMS scheduling failure incrementing retryCount, success after a retry, deletion at the retry threshold, non-SMS reminders not being deleted, and concurrent increments not losing failures.

Unwrapped auth OR can bypass appended filters

In `getBaseConditions`, when `filterConditions` is null the method returns `authConditions` unchanged. For org/team scope that value is an unwrapped OR chain, e.g. `(team match) OR (user match)`. A caller that appends another predicate (`WHERE ${base} AND startTime > ...`) gets SQL where the appended predicate binds only to the last OR branch; rows from the team-booking branch can bypass the added filter. This differs from the old `findMany`, which combined conditions through Prisma's `AND` array. Wrap the returned auth fragment (and the filter fragment) in parentheses so the base condition is self-contained.

Event-type filter fragment is an unparenthesized OR

The event-type filter is built as `(eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)` without outer parentheses. `getFilterConditions` is public and previously returned a grouped Prisma `AND` object, so code that composes it as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}` will evaluate as `auth AND eventTypeId = ... OR eventParentId = ...`; eventParentId rows bypass the auth predicate. Wrap the OR fragment in parentheses at construction.

Public findMany API removed without updating consumers

The public `findMany` method is removed, and `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions` now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of Prisma `WhereInput`. No caller is updated in this PR. Any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, or code that passes these conditions to Prisma's `where`, will fail to compile or query incorrectly. Update all consumers or keep a compatibility method.

Org-scope test depends on unspecified DB array ordering

This expectation compares the `Prisma.sql` values arrays in a fixed order: `[orgId, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. The service obtains these arrays from `findAllByParentId` and `findAllByTeamIds` without an `orderBy`, and `ANY(array)` is order-insensitive. PostgreSQL does not guarantee row order, so the test can fail nondeterministically. Sort arrays before binding/comparison or compare as sets.

Caching behavior no longer covered

The service still caches authorization and filter conditions via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, but this PR deletes both caching tests and adds no replacement. A regression where conditions are rebuilt on every call, or where a cached `null` filter result is not reused, would no longer be detected. Re-add caching tests using spies/call counts.

Team/org ANY conditions never executed against the database

The only integration test that actually executes SQL uses user-scope conditions, which contain no `= ANY(${array})` parameters. The team/org tests only compare generated `Prisma.sql` objects. Array parameter binding and SQL validity for the team/org authorization branches are therefore unverified; a broken `ANY` binding or malformed OR composition there would still pass the suite. Add an integration test that executes org/team base conditions against the database.

Minimum token schema does not allow the fields it is meant to accept

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]`; both computed properties resolve to the same string and the second overwrites the first, so this is not a catchall. The next `if` then sets `refresh_token` to the literal string `'refresh_token'` whenever it was stripped. Schema choice is based on env, not on whether the sync endpoint was used

Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it

`prisma.credential.update` is called here, but this file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This is a TypeScript/build error for the Salesforce app. Add the import or remove the DB write.

Zoom sync request uses the wrong app slug

`refreshOAuthTokens` sends `appSlug` to the credential sync endpoint. Zoom's app slug is `zoom` (the callback creates credentials with `appId: 'zoom'`), but this call sends `zoomvideo` (the folder name). The self-hosted endpoint will not find or sync the correct app. Use `zoom`.

Updated credentials do not clear the invalid flag

This PR adds an authenticated webhook that writes credentials and changes token refresh behavior across many integrations, but no tests cover missing/invalid secret, malformed encrypted payload, update vs create, invalid-flag recovery, fallback when the sync endpoint is absent, or provider-specific response parsing. false_positives.candidate:
One SendGrid cancellation error blocks all other cancellations

The entire cancellation loop is covered by one try/catch. If client.request fails for one reminder, execution jumps to the catch, so no later reminder in remindersToCancel is processed, and the Prisma delete promises already collected in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited. A single stale or failed batch_id can therefore leave many cancelled reminders active and allow their emails to be sent; successfully cancelled rows also remain in the database. Cancellations should be handled per reminder (or with allSettled), and rows should be deleted only after their own cancellation succeeds.

Cron window does not guarantee cancellation for imminent reminders

The cron only picks up cancelled reminders whose scheduledDate is at or before now + 1 hour, but the job runs every 15 minutes. A reminder cancelled just after a cron run and due in, say, 5-10 minutes will not be visited until the next cron run, after SendGrid has already sent the email. The one-hour lookahead does not fix near-term cancellations by itself; imminent reminders need immediate cancellation or a processing mechanism that can run before their send time.

No test coverage for new cancellation lifecycle

No tests were added for the new cancelled flag, the cron cancellation/deletion flow, or the reschedule cancellation path. The previous implementation was wrong without being caught, so regressions here will silently send workflow emails again. Coverage should include: marking a reminder cancelled, the cron cancelling and deleting it, SendGrid failure behavior, reminders without referenceId, and rescheduled bookings cancelling old reminders.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email comparison is case-sensitive and duplicates within input are not removed

`uniqueGuests` filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, but the blacklist is lowercased while `guest` is not, and the existing-attendee comparison is case-sensitive. As a result: (a) a guest whose email differs only in casing from an existing attendee is added as a duplicate attendee row, and (b) a blacklisted address can be added by changing its case. Additionally, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, so duplicate emails within one request are all inserted (the uniqueness check `uniqueEmails.size === emails.length` exists only in the client dialog). Normalize emails (trim + lowercase) before all comparisons and dedupe/validate uniqueness server-side.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says the blacklist is lowercased while the guest email is not, so a blacklisted address can be added by changing its case. That is the same bypass the golden comment describes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||

isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both a team admin AND a team owner at the same time. A team admin who is not the owner (the exact case the variable name and the `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && ...` guard below are meant to allow) fails this check and is rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking. The two predicates should be OR'd, otherwise team admins (excluding owners) cannot use the feature.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: the team admin/owner permission check uses && where it should use ||. The candidate also describes the resulting impact (admins who are not owners get FORBIDDEN), which is consistent with the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sendAddGuestsEmails is passed raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`

Emails are sent with `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the unfiltered input list. If a submitted email already belongs to an existing attendee (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), that attendee matches the `newGuests.includes(...)` branch in `sendAddGuestsEmails` and receives a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` booking confirmation instead of the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification, potentially re-sending the event/ICS to someone who was already on the booking. It should use `uniqueGuests` so only genuinely new attendees are treated as new.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. sendAddGuestsEmails checks newGuests.includes(attendee.email) against the raw guests input array, so existing attendees can be misclassified as new guests. The candidate says the same thing more specifically: guests should be replaced with uniqueGuests.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

Email comparison is case-sensitive and duplicates within input are not removed

`uniqueGuests` filters with `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, but the blacklist is lowercased while `guest` is not, and the existing-attendee comparison is case-sensitive. As a result: (a) a guest whose email differs only in casing from an existing attendee is added as a duplicate attendee row, and (b) a blacklisted address can be added by changing its case. Additionally, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, so duplicate emails within one request are all inserted (the uniqueness check `uniqueEmails.size === emails.length` exists only in the client dialog). Normalize emails (trim + lowercase) before all comparisons and dedupe/validate uniqueness server-side.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that duplicate emails within one request are not deduplicated server-side and are all inserted. This is the same issue as the golden comment. The candidate also raises additional case-sensitivity concerns.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails settings

Unlike every other send* function in this file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` never checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (nor the `eventTypeMetadata` argument). Hosts or attendees who configured `disableStandardEmails` will still receive organizer/attendee emails when guests are added, violating their explicit email preferences. The function should accept and honor the event type metadata like `sendLocationChangeEmails` etc. do.
true_positives.reasoning: Both say sendAddGuestsEmails fails to check the disableStandardEmails metadata flags, so hosts and attendees get emails even when standard emails are disabled. It is the same issue.

false_positives.candidate:
No booking status check before adding guests and sending invites

The booking is fetched by id only and the handler never inspects `booking.status`. Guests can therefore be added to a CANCELLED (or REJECTED) booking and to bookings whose start/end time is in the past. This inserts new attendee rows, calls `updateCalendarAttendees`, and sends `sendAddGuestsEmails` (with a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST) for an event that no longer exists/is over, which is misleading to recipients and pollutes data. The handler should reject non-active bookings (e.g. only ACCEPTED/PENDING and upcoming).

Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials, not the booking owner's

`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the credentials of the user invoking the endpoint, and those are handed to `new EventManager(...)` for `updateCalendarAttendees`. When the caller is a team admin or an attendee (both permitted above) rather than the booking owner, the calendar/video event that must be updated lives on the organizer's connected account, so the update may fail or target the wrong calendar/meeting. The credentials should be resolved for the booking's owner (e.g. `booking.user`) whose calendar holds the event.

Email failures are silently swallowed with console.log

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, dropping the error entirely. Any failure to notify guests/attendees/hosts (e.g. mailer misconfiguration) is invisible in logs/monitoring, so the feature can silently stop sending notifications. Use the project logger and include the error, consistent with the rest of the emails package.

Invalid-email state and input are not reset when the dialog reopens

`isOpenDialog`/`isInvalidEmail` and `multiEmailValue` are only reset on success or on the Cancel button. The Dialog's `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` does not clear `isInvalidEmail`, so after an invalid submission the user closes and reopens the dialog, the red `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error is still shown even though they haven't submitted again; stale entered emails likewise persist. Reset these states when the dialog opens/closes.

New addGuests handler has no tests

The PR introduces a new backend mutation that performs access-control checks, guest deduplication/blacklisting, attendee creation, calendar updates, and email dispatch, plus new email templates, but adds no automated tests. Given the permission check bug and the deduplication/normalization issues above, at minimum unit/integration tests covering authorization (owner, admin, attendee, unrelated user), duplicate/blacklisted/case-variant emails, and cancelled bookings are needed to prevent regressions.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One-time backup codes can be reused concurrently

Consuming a backup code is implemented as a read-modify-write of the encrypted backup-code array: the request reads `user.backupCodes`, finds the matching index, sets that element to null, and writes the entire array back. Two concurrent login requests using the same code can both read the original array and both write their own nulled copy, so both requests succeed and the supposedly single-use code is accepted twice. Use a transaction/row lock or an atomic conditional update keyed on the ciphertext that was read so only one request can consume a given code.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same race condition: the read-modify-write of backup codes lets concurrent logins reuse a single one-time code.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code login can bypass password verification

The new backup-code branch is entered whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, but the password check above only runs when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. This branch never validates `credentials.totpCode`, so an attacker who knows a valid backup code can POST credentials containing the victim email, the backup code, and any arbitrary non-empty `totpCode` (for example `000000`) without the password. Password verification is skipped, the backup code is accepted, and the attacker is logged in. A backup code must not replace the password factor; verify the password whenever backupCode is supplied, or explicitly validate only the selected factor while still requiring the password.

Closing backup-codes screen via dialog X skips onEnable and loses codes

After `handleEnable` succeeds, 2FA is already enabled on the server and the modal switches to `DisplayBackupCodes`. Only the explicit Close button calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()`. Closing via the dialog's X, Escape, or outside click calls `onOpenChange` directly, so the settings switch is not updated, the component can reopen on the stale backup-codes step, and the user may leave without ever seeing or saving the only copy of the backup codes. Any dismissal while on `DisplayBackupCodes` should either commit the enable state and reset state, or be blocked until the user confirms they have saved the codes.

No coverage for actual backup-code login, consumption, or disable flow

The added e2e assertions only check that the download has the expected filename and that a copy-success toast appears; the file contents and clipboard contents are explicitly left as TODO. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, rejects an invalid code, verifies a used code cannot be reused, or disables 2FA using a backup code. These are the security-critical paths added by this PR, and a regression in code formatting, one-time consumption, or either server endpoint would currently pass the tests.

Copy button shows success toast even when clipboard write fails

`navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that can reject when clipboard permission is denied or the API is unavailable, but the promise is neither awaited nor caught and the success toast is shown unconditionally. Users can be told the backup codes were copied when nothing was copied, or an unhandled rejection can be produced. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves, with an error fallback.

Password visibility toggle is ineffective after switching to PasswordField

`PasswordField` sets its own `type` based on `isPasswordVisible` before spreading `{...props}`, so passing `type="password"` here overrides that dynamic value. Clicking the eye button changes the visibility state but the input remains `type="password"`, making the newly added visibility control non-functional in the enable-2FA modal. Remove the explicit `type` prop when using `PasswordField`, or change `PasswordField` so caller props cannot override its visibility-driven type.

Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard navigation

Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the password visibility button removes it from the keyboard tab order. Keyboard-only users can no longer focus the control to reveal or re-hide the password, which is an accessibility regression for every `PasswordField` in the application. Keep the button focusable, or provide an equivalent keyboard-accessible way to toggle visibility.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to the same falsy value

When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which only matches a destination whose externalId is null/undefined. For legacy references without an externalCalendarId this leaves `calendarId` undefined in `updateEvent` (the update fails) and falls back to primary in `deleteEvent` (line 317), deleting from the wrong calendar. Use a real fallback destination or require the external id.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same faulty lookup: find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) compares against the value being searched for, so it never produces a useful fallback. The golden comment frames it as searching for a calendar that matches itself. The candidate frames it as only matching a falsy value when the id is missing. These are different angles on the same logic error in the same code.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unrelated inversion of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED changes organization slug creation

This unrelated change flips the condition: previously `slug` was set when team billing was disabled and `requestedSlug` when enabled; now `slug` is set when billing is enabled, and neither field is set when billing is disabled. That changes organization URL/slug behavior for self-hosted/billing-disabled deployments and is unrelated to the calendar fix. If not intentional, revert it.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for setting slug was inverted. As a result, slug is now set when billing is enabled, and neither slug nor requestedSlug is set when billing is disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stale credential reused when a reference's credential is missing

`credential` is declared outside the reference loop. If a reference has a credentialId that is not in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup fails or yields no app slug, the variable still holds the previous reference's credential and is passed to `updateEvent` with the current reference's uid/externalCalendarId. This can update/delete the wrong host's calendar. Reset `credential` per iteration and skip/report when it cannot be resolved.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments concern the credential lookup failing when reference.credentialId is set but no credential is found, which leaves an invalid credential being passed to updateEvent. The golden comment frames the bad value as undefined. The candidate frames it as a stale credential carried over from the previous loop iteration. That is the same root cause at the same location, with a closely related consequence, so this counts as a semantic match.

false_positives.candidate:
Crash when Google Meet has no destination calendar

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then dereferenced with `.integration`. For a Google Meet event with no destination calendar (null or empty array), it is undefined, so booking creation throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining/defaulting here.

Video meeting references lose credentialId

For non-calendar results (the dedicated video meeting), `credentialId` is now hard-coded to `undefined`. The previous code used `result.credentialId`, which is how the video credential was persisted on the booking reference. Since `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, this regression leaves video meetings behind on cancellation and breaks later video updates.

Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when no main destination exists

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so other collective hosts' destination calendars are never added and those hosts do not get calendar events. Initializing to `[]` has to be done carefully so the organizer's fallback-calendar path is still preserved.

updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId/credentialId

`referencesToCreate` reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` returns an EventResult without either field. Before this change the code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`. Now location changes persist new booking references with both values undefined, so later updates/cancellations cannot locate the actual calendar and credential.

Legacy destination without credentialId loses externalCalendarId on references

When a destination calendar has no credentialId, this branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the destination's externalId. `EventManager.create` now builds `referencesToCreate[].externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId`, so it is undefined even though the destination identifies a specific calendar. Previously the reference used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so this can make later update/delete target the primary or wrong calendar. Pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

Office365 create ignores credentialId and always uses the first destination

`createEvent` always uses `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. EventManager invokes it once per destination credential; for a second collective host, the first host's calendar id is used with the second host's token, usually causing a 404 or writing to the wrong calendar. The same first-only pattern exists in larkcalendar and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts. CalDAV is especially dangerous: filtering the second host's calendars against the first host's externalId can produce an empty list and return success without creating anything.

Recurring collective cancellation still only deletes the organizer's calendar events

The new outer loop over all calendar references enters the recurring branch, but inside it ignores the current `calendarCredential`/`calendar` and iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's credentials only). It also uses `.find` to pick only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. For a recurring collective booking, other hosts' calendar events are never deleted, and the same deletion work is repeated once per current reference. Use the current reference's credential and iterate all references.

Collective confirmation flow does not load all hosts' destination calendars

This handler creates calendar events for bookings that required confirmation. It builds `destinationCalendar` from the single booking destination or the confirming user only, and `handleNewBooking` persists only the first destination on the booking. Other collective hosts' destination calendars are never loaded, so confirming a collective booking still creates events for only one host. The same gap exists in the payment webhooks (`features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts` and `paypal-webhook.ts`), which also create calendar events after payment.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async forEach drops calendar/video deletion promises during reschedule

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` does not await the async callback. Because `getCalendar` is now awaited inside it, the callback suspends before calling `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, so `Reschedule` can return before those integrations have run. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections from the callback either, so calendar/video events may remain after a reschedule and errors become unhandled rejections. Use `for...of` with `await` or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: forEach with async callbacks leaves the calendar/video deletion promises unawaited, so the surrounding try/catch cannot catch their errors and rejections go unhandled. Both recommend for...of or Promise.all as the fix.

false_positives.candidate:
requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` is not awaited. With the new `await getCalendar(...)`, the callback suspends before invoking `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, so `requestReschedule` proceeds to send the reschedule email and return while cancellations are still pending. Any rejected calendar/video deletion is also unhandled. This can leave old calendar/video events active after the user has been told the reschedule request succeeded. Await the callbacks via `for...of` or `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.
